title: Changing where memory updates occurred shifted model retrieval accuracy
summary: Across 24 update schedules with the same number of updates, a 760-million-parameter language model’s retrieval accuracy ranged from 19.7% to 34.2% on the same 6,000 prompts. The test varied which layer groups updated most often while holding the checkpoint and evaluated prompts fixed.
ai_technology: Memory-as-Context MAC-760M; scheduled learned memory updates

evidence.tested: The authors enumerated assignments of four update periods to four fixed layer bands and compared accuracy on each of the same exact-retrieval items.
evidence.unknown: The response range applies to one checkpoint and one retrieval task. The best and worst schedules were identified retrospectively; the ranking need not transfer.
evidence.ai_role: The learned model updated its persistent memory during the task. Controlled placement and frequency changes tested the effects of the same update count on retrieval.
